claims.summary: For any smooth dimension-four root curve C over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, every d>=2 and each of its five inertia elliptic quotients pi_i:C->E_i with pi_i*O_C=O_Ei plus B_i^-1, put eta_i=B_i(-4q_i) at the image of a branch point and epsilon_i,m=1 iff eta_i^m is trivial. Eta_i is nontrivial; s_i,d=epsilon_i,d+epsilon_i,d-1 belongs to {0,1}. The ramification weight of the complete pluricanonical series |dK_C| at each of the eight points over branch value i is 6+2s_i,d. The remaining ramification divisor descends along the degree-16 root cover to a divisor of degree 20d^2-20d-10-sum_i s_i,d, between 2lambda_d-5 and 2lambda_d, lambda_d=10d^2-10d-5. For each fixed d the upper value holds on a nonempty Zariski-open set.
claims.assessment: Working proof by complete-series Riemann-Roch, even/odd local orders on the five elliptic double quotients, the dimension-three degree-one torsion exclusion and the Wronskian line bundle. It counts weights only: no simplicity, polar/colon partition, residual speciality bound or positive-characteristic extension is claimed.
claims.rationale: An all-degree exact branch correction develops the ramification bridge. It identifies the available weight away from branch fibres but does not settle the first-step threshold; novelty beyond the existing quadratic count is not claimed.
claims.next_action: Test specialization of the ramification budget in a two-pair degeneration, retaining component/node corrections and distinguishing polar/colon contributions.

relationships: Uses the smooth genus-five curve, canonical infinity divisor and complete pluricanonical series in dimension four.
Uses the elliptic double-cover splitting and degree-four trace eigensheaf.
The degree-one determinant excludes trivial eta at the quotient mark, which is unramified on the elliptic root cover.
The d=2 generic total agrees with the earlier quadratic separated count; neither statement asserts simplicity from total degree.
Its moving-mark identity explains how the count bears on the polar boundary, without identifying residual contact multiplicities.
